title: [Feature request] Account creation without e-mail address (like on jabber instances)
body:
I would prefer a revised method of creating accounts. If you register a new account on e.g. jabber.ccc.de or jabber.de, it is not required to enter an e-mail address.

I suggest to modify the mastodon code so that this requirement (e-mail address) is dropped and no longer required.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: What about SPAM? there's a lot of SPAM bots on Jabber trying to sell things and it's very annoying. I wonder how do you feel about this issue

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: Requiring a verified e-mail address is an important step for weeding out spam/automated accounts, and it makes creating sockpuppets slightly more tedious. You might be interested in #942 and related issues, i.e. sourcing user accounts from a different database. However, for local sign ups, e-mail will remain a required component.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: Too late. This issue was closed. But I suppose that collecting e-mail addresses is serious privacy violation, especially if the administrator of instance is just a hobby hacker. Sign up without mail is good choice to some instances.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: @hakaba-hitoyo This ("privacy issue") is why I filed the issue.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
Hey, all we need have already been in the configuration: just rewrite 2 lines in devise.rb (and some more changes).
https://theboss.github.io/blog/2018/01/09/mastodon-allow-unconfirmed-email/

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body:
Whether to allow users register without email should be determined by the instance admins, not hardcoded in the software.

Not having a way to disable email requirement is the biggest reason why I no longer use Mastodon.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: It is up for us who write software to decide what the software does, and it is up to you to decide if you want to use it. E-mail is the centerpiece of authentication in Mastodon from day 1 and requiring e-mail confirmation is an important feature that benefits the fediverse, as any server that does not require it would become a vector for spam for everyone else in the network (see the 10minutepleroma incident). So yes, it sounds like Mastodon is not for you.

scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.
